entries.title: SKEET pods and VANE bladed fliers, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. A horizontal shoot-'em-up encounter over the rim of a blue planet: a cluster of SKEET pods drifts in from the right — small armored seed-shaped drone pods with a single magenta eye-slit and stubby fin pairs, matte gunmetal shells with rust-violet panel seams — escorted by VANE bladed fliers, crescent-mirror wingblades spinning around a compact steel chassis, each throwing a thin colored glint as it rotates. Below them the planet's limb curves across the frame, green-teal terrain shelves and ice caps under a thin atmosphere haze, deep navy space above lifting from near-black blue to midnight blue with sparse pixel stars. The two prototype fighters, a sleek steel-blue dart with a bold blue hull stripe, cyan canopy and orange engine glow, enter from the left edge trailing bright cyan tracer fire. Enemy bullets are pink and red orbs with bright cores and dark rims. Lifted deep-navy background, never pure black. Ultra-detailed, large-format, clean vector shapes with pixel-art texture accents.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text artifacts, watermark, blurry, pure black background, human figures, ten wings, morphed silhouettes
entries.notes: flux.2-dev holds two distinct enemy species in one scene without merging them. Color reference: terrain #8ad0a8, stripe #3858f0, canopy #38c8e8, glow #f89830, bullets #ff5aa0/#ff3a3a. Watch that vane blades stay crescent, not full circles.

entries.title: SKEET pods and VANE bladed fliers, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. Close-quarters ambush in the upper atmosphere of a blue planet: three SKEET pods — armored seed-shaped drones with matte gunmetal hulls, rust-violet panel seams and a single glowing magenta eye-slit — crack open mid-flight, hatches folding like petals as they release fan spreads of small pink bullet-orbs with bright cores and dark rims. Two VANE bladed fliers slice through the foreground, steel chassis wreathed by spinning crescent-mirror wingblades catching rim-light, motion implied by doubled blade ghosts. Behind the formation the planet rim glows with a soft cyan atmosphere line, green-teal continent shapes and white cloud swirls floating in a deep navy starfield that lifts from midnight blue to a lighter dusty blue. Clean vector shapes with pixel-art texture accents, ultra-detailed, large-format, colors saturated but limited, background never pure black.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, extra eyes, blobby organic bodies
entries.notes: Ultra-wide 1536x640 reads like an in-game frame strip, good for website zone sections. sd3.5 handles the bullet-orb repetition well. Keep pods seed-shaped, not round balls.

entries.title: SKEET pods and VANE bladed fliers, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, subtle CRT scanline glow, square vertical poster crop. A heroic low-angle study of a VANE bladed flier: a compact gunmetal drone chassis wrapped by three spinning crescent-mirror wingblades, each blade a polished steel scythe with a lilac glint edge, hovering against a vast soft-focus backdrop of a blue planet's limb — green-teal terrain, white storm swirls, and a thin glowing cyan atmospheric arc cutting the corner of the frame. A single SKEET pod, an armored seed-shaped drone with a magenta eye-slit and rust-violet seams, rides the shadow at the edge of the composition. Sparse pixel stars dot the deep navy gradient sky, lifted never black. The mood is clean, cold and mechanical — an patrol arriving in orbit. Bold flat color shapes, limited palette, ultra-detailed large-format illustration with pixel-art texture accents.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, logo, watermark, blurry, pure black, four blades, insect wings, feathers
entries.notes: Vertical poster crop for social/print. flux.1-dev gives the cleanest hard-edged blade shapes. Color reference: blade glint #c8a0ff accent, atmosphere #38c8e8, planet #8ad0a8.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: SKEET pod, four frames on key green
entries.positive: 16-bit SNES-era video game sprite sheet, pixel art style, crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines, saturated limited palette, a regular grid of four equal cells in two rows of two with even gutters, read left to right and top to bottom, one pose per cell in the listed order, the same subject at the same scale, position and light in every cell, on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, no gradients, no shadows under sprites, no text, no labels, no UI. Subject: the SKEET pod — a small seed-shaped armored drone, matte gunmetal shell with rust-violet panel seams, a single magenta eye-slit and stubby fin pairs. Four frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: hatches closed; hatches cracking open; hatches fully open releasing a pink bullet orb with bright core and dark rim; damaged with one fin sheared. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the pose or state changes between cells. Crisp chunky pixels, consistent scale, a chunky readable form that stays clear at small size.
entries.negative: gradient background, text, labels, numbers, photorealistic, 3d render, watermark, blur, anti-aliased smooth edges, dropped shadows, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: Single-subject sheet (plan R3-01 edit 4): the four SKEET frames in a 2×2 grid. The pink bullet orb is a procedural enemy bullet (bible §5.4), not a sheet sprite — only its moment at the hatch is drawn. Color reference: eye-slit magenta #ff5aa0 family, shell gunmetal, seams rust-violet. Expect to hand-clean cell alignment; regenerate variations before giving up. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: VANE bladed flier, four rotation frames on key green
entries.positive: Retro 16-bit pixel art sprite atlas for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up, all sprites drawn at the same chunky resolution with crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines, a regular grid of four equal cells in two rows of two with even gutters, read left to right and top to bottom, on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, evenly spaced grid, no text and no annotations. Subject: the VANE bladed flier — a steel chassis with three crescent-mirror wingblades showing a lilac glint edge. Four frames, the blades rotating in 90-degree steps through one full clockwise turn. The frames in order: blades upright; blades turned right; blades flat across; blades turned left. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the blade rotation changes. Limited saturated palette of gunmetal greys, steel blue and lilac glint. Crisp pixel clusters, no anti-aliasing, no soft shading.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d, gradients, smooth shading, text, watermark, background scenery, stars, planets, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, cast shadow
entries.notes: Square atlas suits a texture-page mockup. sd3.5 at guidance 5.5 keeps grid regularity. Keep the wingblades crescent, not full circles (the encounter-concept note). Color reference: blade glint #c8a0ff. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: TENDER carrier drone, four bay-state frames on key green
entries.positive: Pixel art sprite sheet, SNES 16-bit arcade game style, a wide horizontal filmstrip of four equal cells in one row with even gutters, read left to right, one state per cell in the listed order, the same subject at the same scale and light in every cell, on a flat solid pure bright green chroma-key sheet background, generous even margins, absolutely no text, numbers or labels. Subject: the TENDER carrier drone, a wide, low flat-bellied gunmetal mothership pod with a clipped delta silhouette, rows of tiny green running lights and an open ventral bay door where stored skeet pods queue nose-down, glowing inside. Four frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: bay closed; bay opening; bay fully open; bay closing after a release. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the bay state changes. Crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines around every sprite, saturated limited palette, chunky readable forms that stay clear at small size, classic cartridge-era crispness.
entries.negative: text, labels, UI, gradient background, photorealistic, 3d render, blurry, anti-aliasing, glow bloom, watermark, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: Landscape strip: one subject across the 1536x640 canvas, easiest layout for extraction. flux.1-dev is the steadiest at "absolutely no text" sheets. The released escort drone is the SKEET art drawn small — the v1 sheet's subject, not a new sprite. Color reference: lights #40d070, shell gunmetal. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.
